extracted.intended_audience: ACUS members, staff, consultants, and members of the public interested in ACUS recommendation procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the procedural steps and standards ACUS follows to produce, deliberate, adopt, and publish recommendations or statements about administrative and regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant engagement approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Chairman, with the approval of ACUS’s Council, engages consultants to study particular administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement of outside consultants requires both the Office of the Chairman's initiation and Council approval; consultants are used to study specific processes or procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive research report with suggested recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants prepare a comprehensive research report accompanied by suggested recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be comprehensive and include suggested recommendations based on the study; occasionally, ACUS staff members prepare these reports in-house.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house staff reports as alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally, ACUS staff members prepare the comprehensive research reports in-house instead of using outside consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When staff prepare reports, they follow the same report-and-recommendation model as consultant-prepared studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee deliberation and adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: After extensive deliberation, committees of ACUS’s voting and non-voting members adopt proposed recommendations for Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees include both voting and non-voting members and are expected to deliberate extensively before adopting proposed recommendations to send forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council review and forwarding with views
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council reviews adopted committee recommendations and forwards the recommendations, with its views, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council transmits recommendations along with its own views or commentary to inform Assembly consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly plenary debate, amendment, and formal adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly typically meets semi-annually in plenary session to debate, amend, and formally adopt the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly consideration occurs in plenary sessions (typically semi-annually) where debate and amendment are expected prior to formal adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of adopted recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: After adoption by the Assembly, ACUS undertakes to implement the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation is an explicit post-adoption responsibility of ACUS; adopted recommendations are acted upon by the Conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference Statements as an alternative product
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion the Conference membership adopts a 'Statement' to express its views on a matter without making a formal recommendation; statements may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements are typically produced by the same process that yields recommendations and serve to present issues, study conclusions, or commentary when a formal recommendation is not made; historically ACUS has adopted 19 such statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in searchable recommendations database
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements (and recommendations) are included in the searchable database of recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted statements are archived and made accessible via the recommendations database for public search and reference.
